My kid threw one tantrum with me at home and one in public. He doesn't anymore. Why? Because I didn't negatively reinforce the behavior. The public issue, I took back a train set that was 100 bucks, and huge, it was on sale for 200 bucks off and my kid wanted this so bad. He threw a fit in the car because we had to go to the store before we could go home. I turned around, told him I was taking the train back, I explained why, and he didn't think I would. I did. He hasn't forgotten. He never will. It was the hardest thing to do as a parent thus far, breaking his heart intentionally to teach him that you can't act that way and get what you want. The other tantrum was at home, and it ended when I told him I would take back the toy we had bought the day before. I keep every receipt from toy purchases, and I post it on the fridge when we get home. He knows this and since I started this practice he doesn't miss behave. I explained to him that Toys are a reward and they have to be earned. This was after he started kindergarten. I then made sure that he knew everything he did, good or bad, has consequences. He understands all this because of the actions I took with the train set. He can make the tangible connection between acting bad and having something taken away.

Now my kid still acts out and up from time to time, but never a full on melt down tantrum.
